decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark: enter a web address” and “Invalid/empty addresses are rejected.” Round 1 client approves the saving flow.
decisions.note: Specification gate: saving through a required URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: title is “auto-derived if blank,” while the stated bookmark fields omit description, favicon, and preview image. Round 1 client generally approves without identifying the missing metadata.
decisions.note: Specification gate: automatic collection was narrowed to title rather than all required page metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker promises “see all bookmarks,” but the stated field set lacks description and favicon required for each readable list item. Round 1 client generally approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the presented schema cannot expose all required per-item information.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “search by keyword across title/address/tags.” Round 1 client approves without addressing the omission of description and note from full-text search.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the explicitly listed search fields differ from the required title, description, note, and URL fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: bookmarks are shown “newest first.” Round 1 client approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: newest-first is a conforming sort-key choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits correction/editing to “title/tags/note,” and the stated bookmark fields omit description. Round 1 client approves without mentioning description editing.
decisions.note: Specification gate: editable description, including before and after saving, is absent from the presented model and edit scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents editing as “title/tags/note,” despite address being a bookmark field. Round 1 client approves without discussing URL editing.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the presented edit scope omits URL editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “delete with a confirmation step.” Round 1 client approves the deleting flow.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bookmark deletion is provided; confirmation is an additional compatible safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: users can “label bookmarks” and edit tags. Round 1 client approves the organizing flow.
decisions.note: Specification gate: assigning tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: users can “filter by tag.” Round 1 client approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: filtering by a selected tag conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly decides: “No browser import/export in v1.” Round 1 client says the proposed defaults are acceptable but does not itself state or identify the import/export departure.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Netscape-format import and export were explicitly excluded; collective approval is insufficient for accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Duplicate addresses allowed but warned.” Round 1 client explicitly accepts “warning while allowing duplicate addresses.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client expressly accepts allowing duplicates instead of converging to editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker includes an API create operation that rejects invalid URLs and assumes HTTPS when needed. Round 2 client approves the plan.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: URL-based creation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: create “auto-derives title” with “URL fallback”; the data model contains URL, title, note, and timestamps but no description, favicon, or preview image. Round 2 client approves without identifying this difference.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: the design omits most required remote-page metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker repeats “duplicate-warn-but-allow.” Round 2 client says the plan matches the previously approved specification but does not itself restate or identify this departure.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: this is a new plan-level presentation of the duplicate behavior; bare approval does not establish capture.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies Bookmark-to-Tag many-to-many data and tag updates. Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: multiple tag assignment is supported.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies list filtering with `?tag=`. Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: selecting a tag can filter the bookmark collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker's data model omits description and its update operation covers “title/note/tags.” Round 2 client approves without mentioning description editing.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: description cannot be edited before or after saving under the presented design.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Editing a bookmark's URL is out of scope for v1.” Round 2 client explicitly responds: “URL editing can remain out of scope for this version.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: the client expressly accepts the departure from required URL editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker includes delete in the API and “explicit delete confirmation in the UI.” Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: deletion conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports implemented save behavior that validates the address and assumes HTTPS when the scheme is absent. Round 3 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: Implementation review: URL-based saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports that save “auto-derives a title when blank” but reports no automatic description, favicon, or preview-image collection. Round 3 client broadly accepts the version without identifying the difference.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the implemented metadata behavior remains narrower than required.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports the implementation “warns on duplicates without blocking.” Round 3 client says the app matches the approved behavior but does not itself identify this difference.
decisions.note: Implementation review: duplicates remain permitted; prior awareness is not inferred into this later bare acceptance.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents the completed app using the previously defined schema and reports a “newest-first list,” with no description or favicon data available for list items. Round 3 client broadly accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the completed presentation retains a list model lacking required description and favicon exposure.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: implemented “keyword search over title/address/tags.” Round 3 client accepts without mentioning the missing description and note fields.
decisions.note: Implementation review: full-text search remains restricted to the wrong field set.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports a “newest-first list.” Round 3 client accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Implementation review: this is a conforming date-added sort choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports edit support only for “title/note/tags”; description is not part of the implemented fields. Round 3 client broadly accepts without identifying the missing description editing.
decisions.note: Implementation review: required description editing remains absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “URL intentionally not editable.” Round 3 client accepts the version without itself restating or identifying that departure.
decisions.note: Implementation review: this later implementation-level decision is divergent; prior explicit acceptance does not turn the current bare approval into a captured response.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports delete “behind an explicit confirmation.” Round 3 client accepts the delete flow.
decisions.note: Implementation review: deletion conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports users can “assign tags.” Round 3 client accepts the organizing flow.
decisions.note: Implementation review: tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports users can “filter the collection by a tag.” Round 3 client accepts the organizing flow.
decisions.note: Implementation review: tag filtering conforms.
